answer:
| Feature | Type I Superconductors | Type II Superconductors |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Behavior** | Soft superconductors; exhibit complete Meissner effect. | Hard superconductors; partial Meissner effect. |
| **Critical Fields** | Have a single sharp critical magnetic field ($H_c$). | Have two critical fields: lower ($H_{c1}$) and upper ($H_{c2}$). |
| **Vortex State** | Does not exist. | Magnetic flux penetrates in quantized vortices between $H_{c1}$ and $H_{c2}$. |
| **Examples** | Pure metals (e.g., Aluminium, Lead). | Alloys and transition metal compounds (e.g., $Nb_3Sn$). |
proTip: Highlighting the presence of two critical fields ($H_{c1}$ and $H_{c2}$) in Type II distinguishes it clearly in exams.
